product_overview: Nexora is a secure, token-efficient coding agent for small Python repositories. It analyzes tasks, builds bounded context, runs policy-checked sandbox execution, and returns a reviewable patch with visible evidence.
core_goals: Turn a natural-language coding task into a verified patch with tests and evidence
Enforce deterministic policy controls for every tool action, approval, and sandbox execution
Limit context to relevant repository evidence while preserving security-relevant details
Provide transparent model routing, run state, audit history, and failure reasons
Support a small set of owned Python workspaces and end-to-end run management via API

features.name: Workspaces API
features.description: Lets users list available workspaces and create a new workspace for a coding task.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/workspaces -> Receive 200 with a WorkspaceList of authorized workspaces -> Select a workspace for a run
POST /api/v1/workspaces with valid workspace data -> Receive 200 with a Workspace object -> Use returned workspace for subsequent runs
GET /api/v1/workspaces with invalid or unauthorized access context -> Receive an error response such as 401 or 403 -> No workspace data is returned
POST /api/v1/workspaces with malformed payload -> Receive 4xx validation error -> Workspace is not created

features.name: Runs API
features.description: Creates and starts execution runs for coding tasks within a selected workspace.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/runs with workspace_id, revision, task, acceptance criteria, autonomy, routing mode, and budgets -> Receive 200 with a Run record -> POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/start -> Receive 200 with updated Run state

POST /api/v1/runs with a valid workspace and task -> Receive 200 with a queued/planning Run -> User reviews the plan and starts the run via POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/start -> Receive 200 with the run moved into execution
POST /api/v1/runs with missing required fields or invalid budget values -> Receive 4xx validation error -> No run is created
POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/start for a nonexistent, unauthorized, or already terminal run -> Receive 4xx or 403 error -> Run state remains unchanged
